name: Adalimumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks (some indications weekly) by pre-filled pen or syringe
originator: BASF Knoll with Cambridge Antibody Technology

discovery.by: Cambridge Antibody Technology and BASF Knoll
discovery.note: Isolated by phage display (guided selection from a murine antibody); the first fully human monoclonal antibody approved.

tagline: Fully human anti-TNF antibody, long the world's best-selling medicine
summary: Adalimumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody against TNF-α, given by subcutaneous injection. It treats rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa and uveitis, and as Humira was the top-selling drug in the world for most of the 2010s.
mechanism: Adalimumab binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF-α and blocks its interaction with the p55 and p75 TNF receptors, reducing downstream NF-κB activation and inflammatory mediators such as IL-6 and matrix metalloproteinases.
As an IgG1 it can also lyse cells expressing surface TNF in the presence of complement. Clinically this reduces synovial inflammation, joint damage, gut inflammation and psoriatic skin lesions.
uses: Ankylosing spondylitis and non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis
Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis (adults and children)

history.title: Phage display origin
history.detail: Cambridge Antibody Technology and BASF Knoll begin developing D2E7.

history.title: Abbott acquires Knoll
history.detail: Abbott Laboratories buys Knoll from BASF, gaining the antibody.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in December as Humira for rheumatoid arthritis.

history.title: Crohn's disease
history.detail: Approved for Crohn's disease; psoriasis follows in 2008.

history.title: AbbVie
history.detail: Humira passes to AbbVie, spun off from Abbott.

history.title: Hidradenitis suppurativa
history.detail: First drug approved for hidradenitis suppurativa.

history.title: EU biosimilars
history.detail: Several biosimilars launch in Europe in October, sharply cutting prices.

history.title: US biosimilars
history.detail: Amjevita launches in January as the first US biosimilar, followed by several others during the year.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Serious infections (including tuberculosis, invasive fungal and opportunistic infections) and malignancy, including lymphoma.

facts: It was the first fully human monoclonal antibody approved by the FDA.
AbbVie built a large patent estate around Humira, delaying US biosimilar entry until 2023, about five years after Europe.
